# Application

Runtime facts and controls. F5 adds the CPU clock, the system language, the confirm button and the pause event.

Availability: **PSX** yes | **PSP** yes | **PS2** yes

`Application` already had `Quit`, `isPlaying`, `targetFrameRate` and `platform`. These members are new.

## Members

| Member | PSX | PSP | PS2 | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `static bool SetCpuClock(int mhz)` | no | yes | no | PSP: 222 or 333. Returns false when the platform refuses the value or has no such control; PC builds return false and change nothing. |
| `static SystemLanguage systemLanguage()` | yes | yes | yes | Unity names (`English`, `French` ...). `Unknown` when the platform does not say; treat it as English. |
| `static bool confirmButtonEast()` | yes | yes | yes | True when the platform confirms with the east face button (some regions of the PSP). Pick the confirm button of your menus with it. |
| `virtual void Behaviour::OnApplicationPause(bool paused)` | yes | yes | yes | Called with true when the game is suspended (power switch, Home menu) and false on resume. |

## Notes

- After a resume the frame clock restarts, so the time spent paused is not one long frame.
- Run slower to save battery: `Application::SetCpuClock(222)` in a menu scene, 333 in play. PPSSPP accepts both and keeps its own clock, so measure on hardware.

## Example

```cpp
void Start() override {
  if (Application::platform() == RuntimePlatform::Psp) Application::SetCpuClock(333);
}
void OnApplicationPause(bool paused) override { if (paused) autosave(); }
```
